- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.3), model often fails to correct downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast mean is significantly above true mean (e.g., >5% over 30d), apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong upward trend but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of true values show strong downward trend, model often misses it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
